findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: @growthbook/mcp
findings.detail: 'growthbook__mcp' launches @growthbook/mcp through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["@growthbook/mcp@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'growthbook__mcp': executes commands + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 1 combination(s) exist where one tool executes commands and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they executes commands and can reach the network, which is remote code execution with a delivery channel rather than a hint of one. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
